newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says debt to shippers won't affect exports.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says debt to shippers won't affect exports.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel, fresh from a rescinded strike threat by workers, faced a new challenge on Wednesday from shippers demanding payment for past services, but the company said there was no threat to exports.

Norilsk spokesman Anatoly Komrakov said Norilsk owed 164 billion roubles to river shippers for deliveries of production supplies and consumer goods over 1995 and 1996, but shippers' threats to block delivery of future supplies would not materialise.
"There is absolutely no question of our payment problems to shippers affecting exports in any way," he said.

He said shippers had threatened to block deliveries of supplies along the Yenisei River to Norilsk's flagship plant but that the situation would be resolved and exports and production would not be affected.
Norilsk gets most its supplies via North Sea routes, where icebreakers can carry supplies more economically than can barges up the Yenisei, which is open only four months out of the year.

Norilsk Nickel, one of the world's leading producers of nickel, platinum group metals and cobalt, reached agreement with workers last month under which labour agreed not to strike in the period to July 1.
